problem: Imitation-learned VLN agents suffer exposure bias. DAgger-style fixes supervise recovery actions from off-track states, which semantically conflict with the instruction (Instruction-State Misalignment). Pure RL explores inefficiently on hard samples.
motivation: Small deviations at inference push agents out of distribution and errors compound in long-horizon VLN-CE. Recovery actions such as turning back contradict instructions like 'walk straight' and confuse language grounding, while sparse-reward RL rarely finds correct paths for hard instructions.
key_idea: Roll back a failed on-policy trajectory to its furthest valid progress point on the reference path and have a geodesic oracle synthesize forward-looking supervision from there. Route proficient samples to GRPO and failed samples to this rectification SFT.
insight: Supervising from a valid historical anchor keeps the visual history consistent with the oracle actions. In Table 3, DAgger reaches SR 57.1 / SPL 50.7 at 114 GPU hours, versus 57.6 / 51.1 at 27 GPU hours for BudVLN. In Table 2, rectification alone raises SR (57.0 to 57.2) but lowers SPL (50.5 to 50.1); adding GRPO restores SPL to 51.1, so the two pathways are complementary. Gains over the StreamVLN baseline are small in absolute terms.
method: Greedy Probe: one deterministic greedy rollout per instruction to test whether the policy has mastered it.
Adaptive Mutual Exclusion routing (GRO): a successful probe goes to the GRPO pathway; any failure trigger goes to the rectification SFT pathway. Only one loss is applied per sample.

GRPO pathway: group of G=4 rollouts (the probe plus 3 stochastic samples at temperature 0.4). Reward = success*(2.0 + λ·SPL) − C_dist·d_remain. Group-normalized advantage, clipped surrogate, KL penalty to a reference policy.

Failure triggers: off-track (>3.0m from reference path or heading error >120°), progress stall (60 steps with no new waypoint), premature stop (>3.0m from goal), forced stop (fails to stop in the goal zone after a grace period).

History-Aware Rollback: take the furthest reference waypoint visited as s_anchor, keep the agent's own observation history up to it, reset the simulator there, and have an oracle geodesic planner generate optimal actions to the goal.
Weighted SFT loss: cross-entropy on the oracle action tokens with weights decaying exponentially from the rollback point (w0=1.0), emphasizing immediate correction.
Training: initialized from StreamVLN pretraining, LoRA on the LLM only, AdamW lr 5e-7, joint R2R-CE + RxR-CE training, no extra data.

setting.training_data: R2R-CE + RxR-CE training splits (joint), following StreamVLN pretraining; no external datasets such as HM3D and no synthetic instructions
setting.observation: monocular RGB only (no depth, odometry or maps)
setting.action_space: low-level discrete actions (FORWARD, TURN LEFT, TURN RIGHT, STOP)
setting.privileged: Training only: geodesic oracle planner and reference path used to synthesize supervision and compute rewards. None at test time.

results: BudVLN reaches R2R-CE val-unseen SR 57.6 / SPL 51.1 / NE 4.74 and RxR-CE val-unseen SR 56.1 / SPL 46.6 / nDTW 63.2 with RGB only. It edges past StreamVLN (SR 57.0, SPL 50.5) and ETPNav on R2R-CE, and exceeds StreamVLN on RxR-CE (SR 52.9, SPL 46.0). Training takes 27 GPU hours versus 114 for DAgger.
limitations: Gains over the StreamVLN baseline on R2R-CE are small (+0.6 SR, +0.6 SPL), with no variance or multi-seed reporting.
Relies on a geodesic oracle, a reference path and simulator resets, so it needs simulator access and cannot be applied directly to real-world data.
Evaluated only on R2R-CE and RxR-CE with a single backbone; the text notes no real-robot tests and gives few hyperparameter details (λ, C_dist).
